context: living spec: none matched (registry covers startup/startup-diagnostics only)
constraint: verified card anatomy block is frozen - actions occupy the existing action area only
constraint: no fabricated material identifiers on the card; real item resolution is the separate unified-card workstream

Living specs: the repo registry (living-specs.yml, enabled) resolves NO capability for this feature surface - resolve-spec-paths.py --changed over the waitlist view model, card XAML, image service and list procedure returned []. Both registered capabilities (startup, startup-diagnostics) match only MTM_Waitlist.Startup/** and Module_Startup/**, so there was nothing to fold and no loaded capability to skip-record.
intent: Make the waitlist workable: handlers can accept, complete and release requests, requesters can cancel their own, and the list leads with the most urgent work.
expectations: Re-implementing the status model, audit trail or transitions - they already exist and are tested
Real material identifier resolution (coil/part number, quantity, stock location) - owned by the unified card and taxonomy workstream
Multi-step handoff after completion - hooks only, no behaviour
A creator Edit affordance with no behaviour behind it
approach: Wire the already-built lifecycle to the screens, with the card in the list as the one surface that offers an action: carry the accept/complete/release/cancel commands and their policy gates on the row so the frozen card reaches them through Order, add a confirm-and-reason prompt seam implemented as a ContentDialog in the composition root, order the list with UrgencyCalculator.OrderMostUrgentFirst off the due value the card already shows, and put the note thread plus the audit history on the read-only detail page, which refreshes itself every 30 seconds while it is open.

decisions.decision: Carry the action commands and gate flags on the SampleOrder row
decisions.why: The card sits inside a DataTemplate whose DataContext is the row, so Order is the only channel that already crosses the template boundary; it changes exactly one XAML file
decisions.rejected: RelativeSource FindAncestor binding (undocumented for WinUI and unused in the repo) or command dependency properties threaded through the card plus six per-type line views

decisions.decision: Add CanViewerHandleRequests to the existing RequestActionPolicy with the handler role set
decisions.why: Keeps the UI gate and the service gate provable against each other and stays pure and unit-testable; the vocabulary already exists in SettingsViewModel and ShellViewModel
decisions.rejected: A new cross-module role-rank service, or an inline literal role check in the view model

decisions.decision: Introduce IWaitlistRequestActionPrompt in the module with a ContentDialog implementation in the composition root
decisions.why: Mirrors the existing ISetupDialogService/SetupDialogService/NoOpSetupDialogService pair, so the dialog is injectable and the unit gates run headless
decisions.rejected: Constructing a ContentDialog inside the view model, which throws without a XamlRoot and puts UI composition in a view model

decisions.decision: Order the list by the same due value the card displays, falling back to created plus the sub-type max-allotted
decisions.why: Keeps the list order and each card remaining-time number from ever disagreeing; GetActiveRequests currently orders by requested time descending, the opposite of most urgent first
decisions.rejected: Sorting inside GetActiveRequests, whose domain records carry no urgency state, or adding a new sort helper when UrgencyCalculator already owns the rule

decisions.decision: Revise WaitlistLineCardMarkupTests to assert the action buttons are gated rather than absent
decisions.why: The absence assertion was true only while the buttons were inert; the honest rule now is every button has a Command and a Visibility gate
decisions.rejected: Deleting the check or keeping an assertion that the wired feature must violate

decisions.decision: Show the lost-claim warning as an acknowledgement-required ContentDialog and keep the inline refusal set
decisions.why: Two handlers can claim the same request at the same moment; the loser must be told plainly that another handler took it and to choose a different request, not left looking at an unchanged row
decisions.rejected: An inline message only, which a handler who has already scrolled on may never see

decisions.decision: Read the request back after a refused accept to choose between taken-by-someone-else and gone-from-the-list
decisions.why: Blaming another handler for a request that has left the list would be a false statement about what happened
decisions.rejected: One generic refusal sentence for both cases

decisions.decision: Keep Accept offered to any handler on any unclaimed request
decisions.why: That is the shared-queue design the spec, the seed and OPEN-WORK-NEXT-SPEC 4.3 all require, and it is what makes Release meaningful (a released request goes back so another handler can take it). Runtime evidence confirmed the gate itself is correct: a request claimed by another handler offers no actions at all
decisions.rejected: Restricting Accept to the viewer own requests, which would make the shared list and Release pointless and contradict FR-003/FR-007

decisions.decision: A card keeps its own image when the image resolver answers with its "no image available" placeholder; the resolver only wins when it returns a real image.
decisions.why: Every waitlist_request_types.default_image_path is NULL and config_images_locations is empty, so the resolver could only ever answer with the placeholder - and it did so without saying which answer it was giving, so the card took it over a working image.
decisions.rejected: Returning null from the service (breaks the Settings image dialogs, which legitimately show the placeholder as the effective path); initializing the service at startup (moves the defect to the first load); populating the catalog (a data change hiding a code defect).

decisions.decision: The new-message indicator compares against last_message_utc - the newest NoteUpdated entry that carries an author - rather than the queue row's updated_utc.
decisions.why: updated_utc moves for every lifecycle change, so accepting, completing or cancelling a job flagged the card as though somebody had spoken.
decisions.rejected: Filtering client-side by re-reading each row's audit trail (N extra reads per list load for a value the list query can produce once); keeping updated_utc and suppressing the marker for a recent status change (a heuristic where a predicate will do).

decisions.decision: Writing on a request has no role gate; anyone signed in may send a message.
decisions.why: The box was gated on the handler role, and the people who raise requests are the ones with something to say - the floor could not tell a handler anything.

plan.summary: Plan: wiring-only feature across 2 view models, the row model, the action policy, the card XAML, the detail page, one new prompt seam and its DI line, plus gates G1-G10
plan.key_finding: The entire lifecycle service, policy and urgency math already exist and are tested; GetActiveRequests orders newest-first and GetAuditTrail has no caller, so the gap is purely the missing screen surface

tasks.summary: 30 tasks across Foundational + five user-story phases + Polish, each phase laid out as explicit waves with join lines; no Setup phase because nothing is installed or configured

implement.summary: Wired the lifecycle to the screens, then followed it with four fix passes driven by using the build: the actions live on the card (primary action plus Cancel), the request page reads a request rather than acting on it and refreshes itself every 30 seconds, a new-message indicator marks cards with unread human messages, writing is open to anyone signed in and the history names the sender, Accept and Complete are distinguishable, each status has its own badge colour, and a card keeps its own image instead of the resolvers placeholder. Two database artifacts changed: sp_waitlist_request_audit_list was added and sp_waitlist_request_list gained last_message_utc. Final gates: 0 warnings, 0 errors; 888 passed, 0 failed, 19 skipped of 907.
implement.key_finding: Every defect found after shipping came from the running app, not the unit gates - text lost to a LostFocus binding and a refresh timer, the message marker firing on lifecycle changes, the resolver placeholder overwriting a working image, and the history rendering an event name where a message belonged. Two of them looked like they worked.
implement.risks: Done and Cancelled badge colours are unreachable because the list reads active requests only; no per-request-type image is configured in this database, so card images come from each rows legacy mapping; and the spec is shipped, so its companion journal could not record the post-completion passes.

concerns.note: The running-application pass is read-only by design against live plant data, so the accept/complete/release round trip and the detail page were verified by unit gates rather than by clicking through the app

Two of the three reported defects were invisible to the test suite: a positional DI factory silently dropped optional dependencies, and a view-model await resumed off the UI thread. Both are now guarded where a guard is possible (registration names every parameter) or fixed at the source (no ConfigureAwait(false) in action paths); the thread affinity itself cannot be unit tested without a UI host

The request history is only as complete as the current session: audit rows are written to the store but never read back, so the history block shows nothing for a request the user has not acted on. Recorded as defects/Medium-Waitlist-RequestHistoryShowsOnlyTheCurrentSession.md and left as open task T036 rather than patched, because the read path is a stored procedure that needs live-database validation

Supersedes the earlier read-only-pass note: the request page WAS exercised in the running app after the fixes - a claimed request was opened, its action bar read, Complete invoked through UI Automation, and the outcome confirmed on screen and in the log. The earlier note describes the first pass only

The post-completion passes (T042-T049) could not be journaled: the spec had already reached status=completed and the companion writer refuses to append a task finish to a shipped spec (already shipped; not appending). Their ticks are recorded in tasks.md prose instead, and the exception is declared in that file.

The Done and Cancelled status-badge colours cannot currently be seen: the list is built from GetActiveRequests alone, which returns Pending and Accepted only. They are mapped and tested, but surfacing resolved requests on the list is a product decision.
